title: Open-source NPM package for running in-browser LLMs to power NPCs and agents with zero server costs
author: lordhiggsboson
selftext:
Hi everything, I'm a maintainer for an open-source project called CogentLM

It is an NPM library that you run small LLMs inside three.js/webgl games. Tou can use it to power NPC behavior, generate actions, handle decisions-making, or create dynamic content, all with zero server costs.

We recently launched to NPM if you want to check it out. 

[https://www.npmjs.com/package/cogentlm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/cogentlm)

  
Here’s the demo from the video, along with the source code:

[https://promptcast.dev/](https://promptcast.dev/)

comments.author: DrPaisa
comments.body:
Amazing op will 100% try this out.

Could you download a open source model and package it with your game if it's a offline game with this? What is your creative commons license?

replies.author: lordhiggsboson
replies.body: Yes! You can load any GGUF model at any quant. This could be on HuggingFace or hosted on your own server, both work. License is MIT! Essentially you can do anything with it, commercial or hobby.

Like one that would not hog too much ram basically! 

  
Can't wait to try this out! thanks again

replies.author: lordhiggsboson
replies.body:
np! I like using the LFM 2.5 350M and 1.2B at Q4K\_M quantization. Or the Qwen2/3 ones which are also good. For user text chat / NPC dialog, the 1.2B do pretty well for steering output to match a persona. I use the smaller 350M models for decision making "brain" activity as I can run them continuously and at fast speeds. 

For your game scenario, I think the 1.2B model from LFM or Qwen would work well. I've been easily able to run these on most system, they are about 400MB. But might be able to get away with smaller ones as well.

comments.author: Baphaddon
comments.body: Size of the LLM? Are you using any Bonsai/PRISMLLM models

replies.author: lordhiggsboson
replies.body: I’ve mostly been using either the Qwen2/3 or Liquid LFM models which I find good and my quant of choice is q4K_M. We are working with 1-bit models atm, which should be supported soon. Typical sizes are around 200MB to 400MB. The library also caches the downloads, so future visits don’t require redownloading the model

comments.body: Wait, i understood that we can use Local Llms to get AI behavior, right ? But llms are usually slow even if its 500M. You need to give context qbout how many features ur game supports or what the characters can do then Llm needs to spill out output in a way that ur game can understand.  This is not instant. So,how is this handled?

replies.author: lordhiggsboson
replies.body:
The package provides scaffolding to handle some common game configurations, like characters or a game director/orchestrators. Small LLMs are approaching interactive speeds, with end-to-end response times becoming sub-second. This makes them useful for NPCs, decision making, adding dynamic content, or acting as a game "AI" to provide actions across characters/things. 

The most interesting use cases I've seen involve using an LLM not as a "chatbot" dialogue machine, but as a "brain" for NPC characters or animals, giving them more life-like interactions in the world. 

My view is that utilizing LLMs in games locally is an untapped and underutilized tool that can open up new game modes and mechanics not yet seen today, just waiting for the right game designer to discover and create with.

replies.author: whoishack
replies.body: 20+ year dev here - this is exactly what I've been working on since last year. I wanted to integrate AI but the models are just too large for things like older mobile devices or even browsers on older computers at this time, which is unfortunate. I've now spent the last 5 months almost day and night working on a brain engine algorithm (i hate calling it AI) to function as close to AI without actually needing an LLM and all I can say right now is I wish we were another 2 years in the future as I expect models to eventually get small enough for that.

replies.author: lordhiggsboson
replies.body: Sounds interesting! I think we are at the point where they're small + fast enough to start being useful in certain narrow spaces. I've been playing with models around 200MB which run pretty well and can act as a brain for decision making. The `LFM 2.5 350M` models are pretty good for this, might be worth looking into
